title: Continuum Backup & Recovery Failover Terms — Cloud Failover, DR Tests and the Server-Day Balance
content:
Cloud failover under Continuum Backup & Recovery is available only where the tier includes cloud virtualization. A production failover starts only after the authorized contact signs a production failover authorization where the tier requires that signature; a DR test is scheduled through the account team, counts against the tier's full DR tests per contract year, and its server-days are free where the tier makes DR test server-days free of the balance. Each contract year is granted the tier's annual failover server-days at activation and at each anniversary of the term start date, and unused days are forfeited at the year's end and at closing. Server-days of a production failover are servers multiplied by started calendar days in the cloud; they are drawn from the year's balance and any excess is billed at the tier's failover day rate per server-day.

## Kinds of failover

A failover starts protected servers in the provider cloud, either for a DR test or for a production disaster, and ends with failback to the client's site. Each failover has its own reference, a start moment and an end moment, and the server-days run are recorded when it ends.

| | DR test | Production failover |
|---|---|---|
| Availability | Only where the tier includes cloud virtualization | Only where the tier includes cloud virtualization |
| Start | Scheduled through the account team | Only after the authorized contact signs a production failover authorization, where the tier requires the signature |
| Allowance | Counts against the tier's full DR tests per contract year | — |
| Server-days | Free where the tier makes DR test server-days free of the balance | Drawn from the contract year's balance; any excess billed at the failover day rate |

## The failover day balance

The plan's failover day balance is the cloud failover server-days available in the current contract year. Days are granted for a contract year at activation and at each anniversary of the term start date. Unused days of a contract year are forfeited at that year's end, and the remaining days are forfeited when the plan closes.

The balance that a production failover draws on is the balance of the contract year in which the failover ended: the server-days granted for that contract year, less the server-days drawn by production failovers in it, less the server-days forfeited for it.

## Server-days and the overage charge

**Server-days of a production failover.** The number of servers failed over multiplied by the number of started calendar days in the cloud. Every calendar day on which the servers ran in the cloud counts as a started day, including the day the failover began and the day it ended.

**Overage server-days.** The greater of (a) the failover's server-days less the balance of the contract year in which it ended, and (b) zero.

**Overage charge.** The overage server-days multiplied by the tier's failover day rate per server-day.

**Worked example (hypothetical figures only).** A contract year was granted 10 server-days, of which 4 have already been drawn and none forfeited, leaving a balance of 6. A production failover runs 2 servers from the 3rd to the 6th of a month — the 3rd, 4th, 5th and 6th are 4 started calendar days.

| Quantity | Working | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Server-days | 2 servers multiplied by 4 started calendar days | 8 |
| Overage server-days | The greater of 8 less 6 and zero | 2 |
| Overage charge, at a hypothetical rate of 300.00 USD per server-day | 2 multiplied by 300.00 USD | 600.00 USD |

Had the failover run 1 server for 3 started calendar days, its 3 server-days would be within the balance of 6, and the overage server-days would be zero.
